pr_title: Upgrade Telegram lib, refactor component for breaking changes
pr_body:
<!--

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

This PR upgrades `python-telegram-bot` from 11.1.0 to 13.0 and adjusts the component for breaking changes in the two major version jumps. Overall I tried to improve code quality but to keep the changes minimal and avoid rewriting everything in one PR. But please suggest changes where it makes sense to improve code quality, I'm not an experienced Python developer.

### Changes from 11 -> 12

Transition guide: https://github.com/python-telegram-bot/python-telegram-bot/wiki/Transition-guide-to-Version-12.0

A few handler callback parameters are updated in `polling.py` according to the transition guide.

### Changes from 12 -> 13

Transition guide: https://github.com/python-telegram-bot/python-telegram-bot/wiki/Transition-guide-to-Version-13.0

The only breaking change that affects our component is the [API keyword argument handling](https://github.com/python-telegram-bot/python-telegram-bot/wiki/Transition-guide-to-Version-13.0#api-keyword-arguments). Previously the component passed around arguments for the library `send_something` methods as `**kwargs`, because the library methods accepted arbitrary arguments via the `**kwargs` parameter. This is no longer the case in version 13, so we have to use explicit arguments. There is still too much indirect argument passing for my taste, so I'd like to simplify this in a future PR.

issue_context.title: Context based callbacks for Telegram
issue_context.body:
Migrate the Telegram integration to use [Context based callbacks](https://github.com/python-telegram-bot/python-telegram-bot/wiki/Transition-guide-to-Version-12.0#context-based-callbacks). 

With #27411 you will get a "Deprecation Warning".

review_comments: The `camelCase` methods are just aliases for the `snake_case` methods, so I decided to use the original methods for consistency.

`message_tag` is not a Telegram API parameter, it's just an internal state for the component. Previously it was mixed with all the other params (that were passed to the Telegram API), now this is handled separately.
